title: Unemployment Benefit Claims — Claimant Handbook: Withdrawing a Claim
content:
A claimant may withdraw an Unemployment Benefit Claims record, usually to file a new claim with a later base period or in another state.

## Conditions

1. A claim may be withdrawn only when the net benefits paid on it are zero, meaning that no payment was issued or every payment was cancelled or repaid. Net benefits paid are the payments issued on the claim in its benefit year, less cancelled payments, less the principal repaid, offset, intercepted or waived on overpayments established against the claim.
2. Withdrawal is the claimant's own decision: the agent records a claim withdrawal request in the claimant's name, and the claim is withdrawn only once the claimant confirms it.
3. A claim may be withdrawn only before the benefit year end date of the claim. The withdrawal limit is counted in calendar days, with no grace days (0), and a request on the benefit year end date itself is too late.

The figures read are those on the claim records and the overpayment records established against the claim.

## Both sides of the withdrawal limit

| Day of the request | Withdrawal limit |
|---|---|
| The day before the benefit year end date | In time |
| On the benefit year end date | Too late |

## Effect of withdrawal

A withdrawn claim cannot be reinstated, its waiting week and monetary determination are void, and a claim filed afterwards is determined on its own base period.

### Hypothetical figures

A claim with 600.00 issued, 300.00 cancelled and 300.00 of overpayment principal repaid has net benefits paid of zero and meets condition 1; with only 200.00 repaid, 100.00 remains and the claim may not be withdrawn.
